newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Land Fund stands at about HK$170 bln - Tung.
newsitem.headline: HK's Land Fund stands at about HK$170 bln - Tung.

text.p: Hong Kong's future government will inherit a Land Fund of about HK$170 billion when the territory reverts to Chinese rule, post-handover leader Tung Chee-hwa said on Monday.
The previous officially announced figure for the Land Fund, created in 1983 to hold half of the revenues from government land sales, stood at about HK$150 billion.
Hong Kong reverts to Chinese rule on July 1 and becomes a Special Adminstrative Region (SAR) of China.
"This fortune can give the SAR government ample room to improve our gradually lagging competitiveness," Tung said in a live interview with six local media organisations.
He also noted the territory's Exchange Fund, which stood at HK$534.5 billion at the end of last year, was "definitely enough to stabilise the Hong Kong currency during the transitional period".
